reason: The text contains a highly unfavorable depiction of Aaron in the golden calf episode (Exodus 32). Aaron collects gold from the people, fashions it into an idol calf, and builds an altar before it—leading the Israelites into idolatry and blasphemy. When confronted by Moses, Aaron deflects blame onto the people rather than taking responsibility. While Exodus 19:6 contains aspirational language about Israel becoming 'a kingdom of priests' (ממלכת כהנים), this is idealistic future language, not a favorable depiction of actual priestly conduct. The concrete portrayal of the priest Aaron in action is decidedly negative.
